newsitem.title: THAILAND: THAILAND SEES INFLATION NOT IN DOUBLE DIGITS.
newsitem.headline: THAILAND SEES INFLATION NOT IN DOUBLE DIGITS.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said on Wednesday he did not expect inflation to surge to double digits after Thailand adopted tough austerity measures in an international bailout package sponsored by the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
Thanong, asked if Thailand's decision to raise its value added tax (VAT) would stoke inflation, said: "We should not be over concerned. Inflation will unlikely reach double digits."
The government has announced it would raise VAT to 10 percent from seven percent from August 16 as part of its compliance with conditions in the IMF package.
Thanong said last week when he announced the IMF package that the government would try to restrain inflation to eight or nine percent.
The VAT hike has since triggered a rush of supermarkets by housewives concerned about a possible sharp increase in prices of consumer goods after the increase.

The Thai consumer price index rose about 4.5 percent year-on-year during the first seven months of this year. Analysts expected inflation to rise to at least eight percent during the second half of 1997.
